ads_ratio.reason: Amer Sports is a direct-listed foreign private issuer: one NYSE-traded AS share is one ordinary share, so no ADS conversion applies; per-share figures and the traded price are on the same basis.
ads_ratio.source: Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-26, EDGAR as-20251231.htm, CIK 1988894): the NYSE-listed security is the ordinary share itself — the Description of Share Capital filed with the annual report states 'Our ordinary shares are listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) under the symbol AS', and the company's SEC offering filings (424B4/424B5, CIK 1988894) register Ordinary Shares, not ADSs

moat_against: ROIC proxy only 8.1% in FY2025 and below that in every prior year (fundamentals.json) — no through-cycle record of returns above the cost of capital
Brand-heat / fashion risk: Arc'teryx and Salomon softgoods growth leans on trend demand that can cool; Arc'teryx is drifting toward lifestyle
Greater China concentration (~28% of FY2025 revenue) with intensifying local competition (KAILAS, Anta, Li-Ning outdoor pushes)
Wilson / Ball & Racquet is a low-margin, contested category (segment margin compressed in 2025 prints on tariffs and SG&A)
Controlling-shareholder overhang from the Anta-led consortium ownership structure and repeated primary share issuance
moat_for: Arc'teryx premium technical-apparel franchise with proven pricing power — group gross margin 49.1% (FY2021) to 57.6% (FY2025)
Salomon scale in outdoor performance; softgoods/footwear momentum drove Outdoor Performance +37% in Q2 2026
Wilson's century-old ball & racquet franchise (Tennis 360 ecosystem) adds a second, steadier brand pillar
Rising direct-to-consumer mix (record 55% of revenue in Q2 2026) — controlled distribution, full-price sell-through
Multi-brand platform effect in Greater China: FY2025 Greater China revenue +43.4% to $1.86B
moat_justification: Portfolio of genuinely premium technical brands — Arc'teryx in technical apparel, Salomon in outdoor performance, Wilson in ball & racquet — with demonstrated pricing power: gross margin expanded from 49.1% (FY2021) to 57.6% (FY2025) in fundamentals.json while revenue compounded at ~21-27%/yr, and the direct-to-consumer mix keeps rising. But the measured returns do not yet support a wide moat: the roic_proxy series in fundamentals.json runs -27.9% / 0.7% / 4.0% / 6.7% / 8.1% for FY2021-25 — only just reaching roughly the cost of capital in the latest year, with no through-cycle history above it under the current capital structure. Brand heat in outdoor/fashion is fickle, Wilson and winter-sports equipment are contested, lower-margin categories, and Greater China is a large, concentrated growth engine exposed to local competition (KAILAS, Anta, Li-Ning). Moderate/narrow moat, 5/10.
name: Amer Sports, Inc.
one_liner: Real premium-brand quality, moat 5/10, but the price pays for perfection: weighted IRR 5.4% and weighted IV@15 $6.01 vs $30.02 on the normalized base — even on the latest-FY base ($0.85/sh) the weighted IRR is only 9.3% with IV@15 $14.91; clears 15% only below ~$6.01 on the scored base.
sector: Consumer Discretionary / Premium sporting goods & apparel (Arc'teryx, Salomon, Wilson)
